_comment: Regenerate spec values with: python -m sim_agent101.cameras --write. Calibrated values are written by scripts/sim_calibrate_cameras.py and must not be overwritten by --write (it refuses).

front.source: ChArUco calibration, refined by Nelder-Mead over real renders vs the real overhead frame
front.note: ChArUco gave fx 990.396 fy 996.956 cx 323.496 cy 300.367 (RMS 0.2651 px, 15 views). A 9-parameter silhouette fit over actual Isaac renders moved them to f=991.4, cx=320.7, cy=303.3 -- i.e. it CONFIRMED the calibration, including the 60 px cy offset, rather than replacing it. Paired with OVERHEAD_POS_OVERRIDE in tasks/push_t_env_cfg.py. Omniverse renders square pixels, so fx=fy here; the ChArUco fx/fy differed by 0.7%.

grip.source: Nelder-Mead over real renders, 9 camera parameters, vs the real wrist frame
grip.note: Fitted by rendering the gripper in Isaac across a grid of (f, cx, cy) and scoring each ACTUAL render against the real wrist frame. boundary error 3.1 px, IoU 0.932, against a measured noise floor of ~0.95 (re-thresholding the real frame moves its own mask by 0.94-0.98). Paired with CAMERA_POS_OVERRIDE in assets/objects.py -- the two were fitted together and neither transfers to a different camera pose. Do NOT fit these with a depth-reprojection surrogate: one predicted IoU 0.961 for a pose the renderer then scored 0.339. The surrogate only holds for corrections of a millimetre or two. f is paired with the 24 mm dolly in CAMERA_POS_OVERRIDE and neither means anything without the other -- closer-and-wider is one degree of freedom, fitted on the silhouette's width profile because IoU cannot see it. cx=330 is the one number here that is a real lens property -- it came out ~330 from two camera poses 12 degrees apart, so it is not absorbing pose error. cy is: it fits to 210 at the bore pose and 285 at this one, because a principal-point shift and a camera tilt are indistinguishable from a single view. Treat cy as an image-space correction paired with the pose, not as a measurement of the lens. Superseded: the ChArUco solve (735/695, cx 212 cy 205) scored IoU 0.223. Its distortion coefficients are kept only as the sole estimate available; Omniverse ignores distortion regardless.
